category_title: Students with externalizing behavior problems including work refusal and temper tantrums
minimal_context: The student is seated at a cluster of desks in the TLC classroom and is asked to complete an academic worksheet that increases in difficulty.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please take a pencil from the communal stationery and start on the next section of the worksheet. The questions get a bit harder here.

STUDENT: (Pushes the worksheet away) I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: Why don't you just give it a try?

STUDENT: No. I'm not participating in this.

TUTOR: You need to finish this assignment before the end of class.

STUDENT: (Knocks the communal stationery off the desk cluster) I'm not doing this work! It's too hard and I don't care!

options.A: Publicly celebrate the student's 'new learner identity' as often as possible and communicate this across all learning sites.
options.B: Apply increasingly serious disciplinary measures if the work refusal continues, such as classroom suspension, detention, and school suspension.
options.C: Compromise, negotiate situations, and share decisions and power with the student instead of imposing control over the worksheet.
options.D: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level questions on the academic worksheet based on the student's reading level.
